inspiration: Three tiers of actors by distance to the player: README lines 30-34 describe visible (hot) bots with full detail, out-of-view (cold) bots with a cheaper background simulation that keeps goals and parties, and static bots with no brain. A cold bot is promoted to hot when a player comes near. Idea for row 23 (zone population) and the server tick row 18 sub-line 'per-tick NPC budget': tier each actor by view distance and promote on approach. Keep: the tiers and the promotion rule; change: our tier names and distance thresholds.

A per-tick budget that tightens when a player is online: PopulationConfig.js sets a scheduler slice of 12 ms (line 12), an idle budget of 2500 ms (line 13) and a player budget of 100 ms (line 14), and max resolves per tick of 100 when idle and 12 with a player (lines 16-17). Idea for the server tick: a two-state throttle, not a fixed cap. Keep the two states; change the values to fit our fixed step.

Work with a lease: cold owner lease 30000 ms (line 26), with renewal and recovery intervals. A worker claims a job, renews it, and a lost claim is recovered rather than lost. Idea for background simulation that must not stall the main loop.

Yield to players in flight: the cold worker caps in-flight jobs at 8 while a player is online (line 34) and at 2 when lagging. Idea for the many-on-one case: background work gives way when the fight needs the loop.
Tuning without a code change: each budget has an environment name (line 248 onwards, for example BOT_POPULATION_SCHEDULER_PLAYER_BUDGET_MS). Idea for zone data: caps and budgets set per deployment.

A stat block split into groups: an NPC template splits identity, base attributes, combat stats, speed and vitals (c4_heine.json lines 11, 19, 30, 34 for base, stats, speed and vitals). Idea for row 21 (catalogue fields): group fields the same way so a creature can be read at a glance.
Role tags as data: data/Npcs/ai.json gives each NPC id a role of FIGHTER, ARCHER or BALANCED (line 1). Idea for row 2 (AI brain): a role per creature in data, the brain reads the tag.

Raid bosses with minions: ColdCombatProfile.js line 12 loads a raid boss minion file (data/Npcs/Minions/c4_raid_bosses.json, existence under Minions/ not checked). Idea for boss set pieces: a boss plus a minion list in data, with the minion list held separately.

briefs.label: Tiered crowd band (own label)
briefs.why: Actors near the player are fully simulated and the rest run a cheap background loop; the world feels alive without a cost per actor.
briefs.keep: three tiers by distance; promote from background to full on approach; a background loop that keeps goals
briefs.change: our own tier names and distances (no town traders as a tier); a fight-only tier that is always full; our own promotion rule

briefs.label: Role-tag duelist (own label)
briefs.why: A creature role as one tag (fighter, archer, balanced) changes how it fights without a new brain per creature.
briefs.keep: one role tag per creature in data; three roles; the brain reads the tag
briefs.change: our own role names (for example brawler, skirmisher, sentinel); a silhouette and weapon for each role that differs from the donor's

briefs.label: Minion-led boss set piece (own label)
briefs.why: A boss that brings its own minion list gives a readable phase without a second boss file.
briefs.keep: a boss plus a minion list in data; the minion list is separate; a fight with waves
briefs.change: our boss silhouette and palette; our minion roster; a wave timing of our own
